title: SFO–YVR: Harini Das
notice: Source-reviewed against Canadian government publications on 2026-10-25. Passenger and document data are fictional; no independent human review is claimed.

review.notes: Checked the authored evidence path, exceptions and disposition against ca-student, ca-us-only-return, ca-visitor-visa. See docs/content-review-2026-10-25.md. This is an agent source review, not independent human or immigration-authority approval.

assumptions: Adult passenger on the direct commercial SFO–YVR flight; ordinary genuine documents, matching identity, and all non-document airline checks are stipulated satisfied. No decision here guarantees admission at the Canadian border.

Only the declared citizenship and residence status apply. No unmentioned second passport, US/Canadian permanent-resident status, diplomatic exception, or other travel-permission exception is available.
Passenger names and document numbers are synthetic. Electronic authorization results are simulated carrier checks, never live calls and never a requirement to carry an eTA printout.
The study permit was issued before departure from Canada. The student remains enrolled at a designated learning institution and meets all other study and admissibility conditions.

attributes.status: VALID; attending a designated learning institution

clues: The student has a current Canadian study permit, but the visa expired yesterday. The trip began in Canada and included a holiday before the final US segment. Clarify the travel history and any replacement visa.

questions.label: Clarify trip and current travel permission
questions.response: Since leaving Canada, I visited Japan and then the United States. I have no new Canadian visa or other qualifying permission.

rationale: The student visited Japan as well as the US, so the US-only return exception does not apply. The study permit does not replace the missing valid travel visa in this case. The inquiry confirms no replacement permission.
